I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is still the most reliable way for me to keep output steady and avoid taking unnecessary market and weather risk. I am 60, so I value a system I know well, can manage on time, and can harvest with local machinery without too much trouble. I will put all my main field into winter wheat first and then summer maize on the same land after wheat harvest. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is stable and easier to manage, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is usually better. I will not spread myself across too many crops this year. That would add labor, management difficulty, and sales uncertainty.

For management, I will stay fairly standard and practical. For wheat, I will prepare the land with rotary tillage, apply base fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium, split nitrogen between base and topdressing, irrigate at the key stages, and control weeds and disease with a limited number of sprays rather than spraying too often. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize and use no-tillage sowing to save time and preserve moisture. For maize, I will focus fertilizer around sowing and jointing, irrigate when the field actually needs it, and keep pest control to the main pressure periods. My goal is not chasing the absolute highest yield. I want a stable yield, manageable costs, and a cropping plan I know I can carry through well.
